scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana: Establishment of Backyard mini RAS Units - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana is a flagship scheme initiated by the Government of India to enhance fish production and promote sustainable aquaculture practices across the country. 

This scheme was launched on September 10, 2020. 

It aims to achieve the target of increasing fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-2025. 

The scheme is designed to support the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers while ensuring the sustainability of aquatic resources. 

The establishment of Backyard Mini RAS (Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems) Units in Haryana is a significant component of this scheme. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to promote the establishment of small-scale aquaculture units that can be set up in backyards. 

These units are intended to provide an alternative source of income for rural households. 

The scheme aims to empower women and marginalized communities by providing them with the necessary skills and resources to engage in fish farming. 

The benefits of the Backyard Mini RAS Units include enhanced fish production, improved income levels, and increased employment opportunities. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance of up to INR 2 lakh is provided for the establishment of each mini RAS unit. 

The financial assistance covers 60% of the total cost for general category beneficiaries. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the assistance is increased to 80% of the total cost. 

The mini RAS units are designed to be environmentally sustainable and efficient in water usage. 

Each unit can produce approximately 1,000 kg of fish annually. 

The types of fish that can be cultivated in these units include tilapia, catfish, and Indian major carps. 

The scheme also emphasizes the use of modern technology in fish farming practices. 

Training programs are organized to educate beneficiaries about best practices in aquaculture. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a resident of Haryana. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. 

There is no specific upper age limit for applicants. 

The annual income limit for applicants is set at INR 3 lakh for general category beneficiaries. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, there is no income limit. 

Applicants must also possess a basic understanding of fish farming practices. 

The application process for establishing a Backyard Mini RAS Unit involves several steps. 

First, interested applicants must submit an application form to the local fisheries department. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website of the Haryana Fisheries Department. 

Applicants are required to provide documents such as identity proof, income certificate, and a project proposal. 

The project proposal should outline the proposed unit's design, expected production, and financial requirements. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the fisheries department. 

If approved, the beneficiaries will receive a sanction letter detailing the financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the project. 

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the unit. 

The timeline for establishing a Backyard Mini RAS Unit is generally around six months from the date of approval. 

The Haryana Fisheries Department is the implementing authority for this scheme. 

The department is responsible for providing technical support and guidance to beneficiaries. 

Contact details for the Haryana Fisheries Department can be found on their official website. 

The scheme also aims to promote the consumption of fish as a source of protein among the local population. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to educate the public about the nutritional benefits of fish. 

The establishment of Backyard Mini RAS Units is expected to contribute significantly to the overall fish production in Haryana. 

The state has set a target to increase its fish production to 1.5 lakh metric tons by 2024. 

The scheme is aligned with the National Fisheries Policy, which aims to promote sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. 

The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana is part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

This initiative focuses on making India self-reliant in various sectors, including fisheries. 

The scheme also encourages the use of indigenous fish species to promote biodiversity. 

Beneficiaries are encouraged to adopt eco-friendly practices in their fish farming operations. 

The Haryana government is committed to providing continuous support to beneficiaries through training and capacity-building programs. 

The success of the Backyard Mini RAS Units can lead to the establishment of larger aquaculture farms in the future. 

The scheme is expected to create a multiplier effect in the local economy by generating employment opportunities. 

The establishment of these units will also help in reducing the pressure on natural water bodies. 

By promoting aquaculture, the scheme aims to enhance food security in the region. 

The Haryana government is also exploring partnerships with private sector players to improve the supply chain for fish farming. 

The scheme is expected to foster innovation in aquaculture practices. 

Beneficiaries will have access to market linkages to sell their produce. 

The government is also working on creating a digital platform for fish farmers to connect with buyers. 

The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana is a comprehensive approach to transforming the fisheries sector in India. 

The establishment of Backyard Mini RAS Units in Haryana is a crucial step towards achieving the objectives of this scheme. 

The initiative is expected to uplift the socio-economic status of fishers and fish farmers in the state. 

The government aims to create a sustainable and profitable aquaculture sector through this scheme. 

The success of the Backyard Mini RAS Units will serve as a model for similar initiatives in other states. 

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of rural communities through sustainable practices. 

Overall, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana and the establishment of Backyard Mini RAS Units in Haryana represent a significant investment in the future of aquaculture in India.
